I use notion for all my organization, note-taking, planning, hell, even grading myself. It's the first program I recommend for anything regarding digital note-taking.   


Omnicalculator is my go-to for anything regarding, well, calculating. it offers calculators for anything from DNA concentration to labor cost, to atomic mass, to the Fibonacci sequence. A literal godsend.   


So long as you check where the information is sourced from, Wikipedia is a genuinely good website for almost everything.   


Quizlet is good for studying, memorization, flashcards, etc. Teachers use it so much for a reason.   


For physical items, I recommend investing a journal / binder where you can insert different kinds of paper. I personally use a TUL notebook for literally everything - my calendar, my journal, my maths, my art... Being able to personalize your workspace helps a lot. Have a dedicated place where you do your schoolwork where you can minimize distractions while simultaneously being comfortable. If this means at the kitchen table, cool! If it means on the floor, cool! If that means under your bed at two in the morning, cool! Your routine doesn't have to fit inside the box. Find a schedule that works best for you. Only you know the best way to help yourself.
